questions.question: Which among the following is Phanerogams, flowering and seed - bearing plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gymnosperms.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phanerogams:-**

 
 
• **​**These are plants that produce **flowers and seeds** and are also known as **angiosperms.**
 
 
 
• **Gymnosperms:-**
 
 
• Gymnosperms are a group of seed-producing plants that includes conifers, cycads, Ginkgo, and gnetophytes.
 
• Gymnosperms are known as "naked seed" plants because their seeds are not enclosed in a fruit. Instead, the seeds are exposed on the surface of the plant, often in cones.
 
• Some examples of gymnosperms:
 
 
• Conifers: Pines, firs, spruces, cedars, etc.
 
• Cycads: Sago palms, etc.
 
• Ginkgo: Ginkgo biloba
 
• Gnetophytes: Welwitschia, Ephedra, Gnetum
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pteridophyta :-

 
 
• Pteridophyta, also known as ferns, are a group of vascular plants that reproduce by spores.
 
• They are the first group of plants to evolve vascular tissue, which allows them to transport water and nutrients throughout their bodies.
 
• Pteridophytes are also the first group of plants to have true leaves.
 
 
 
• **Bryophyta**:-
 
 
• It is also known as mosses, liverworts, and hornworts, are a group of non-vascular plants that reproduce by spores.
 
• They are the most primitive group of land plants, and they are found in a wide variety of habitats, including forests, wetlands, and even deserts.
 
 
 
• **Thallophyta**:-
 
 
• It is a polyphyletic group of non-mobile organisms that are traditionally described as "thalloid plants", "relatively simple plants" or "lower plants".
 
• They form a division of kingdom Plantae that include lichens and algae and occasionally bryophytes, bacteria and slime moulds.

questions.question: Cosmic snowballs of frozen gases, rock and dust that orbit the Sun are known as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Comets.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Comets:-**

 
 
• These are **cosmic snowballs** of **frozen gases, rock, and dust** that orbit the Sun.
 
• They have a **coma**, a fuzzy atmosphere of gas and dust that surrounds the nucleus, and a **tail** that points away from the Sun.
 
• Comets are believed to be remnants from the **formation of the Solar System.**
 
• They can have** highly elliptical orbits **and can take hundreds or thousands of years to complete one orbit around the Sun.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meteors:-**

 
 
• These are small rocks or debris that** burn up** upon entering Earth's atmosphere, while **meteorites **are any **surviving pieces** that reach the ground.
 
 
 
• **Stars:-**
 
 
• These are massive, luminous spheres of **plasma** held together by **gravity.**
 
 
 
• **Meteorites**:-
 
 
• These are pieces of rock or metal that have fallen to Earth from space.
 
• They are the only physical evidence we have of what exists beyond our planet, and they can provide valuable insights into the formation and evolution of the solar system.

questions.question: With which country does India share the longest border?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangladesh.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The India-Bangladesh border:-**

 
 
• India shares the longest border with Bangladesh, which is approximately 4,096 km long.
 
• It is also known as the** International Border (IB)** and is divided into three sectors, namely,** Eastern, Central, and Western.**
 
• The India-Bangladesh border is characterized by numerous** rivers and their tributaries**, which act as natural boundaries between the two countries.
 
• The border is also marked by **fencing, pillars, and barbed wires **to prevent illegal immigration, smuggling, and other cross-border crimes.
 
• The India-Bangladesh border is of **strategic importance** to both countries as it connects the northeastern states of India with the rest of the country and provides Bangladesh with access to the** Bay of Bengal.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **China** shares a border with India, which is approximately **3,488 km long.**

 
 
• The India-China border is also known as the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)** and is the subject of a** long-standing territorial dispute** between the two countries.
 
 
 
• **Nepal** shares a border with India, which is approximately **1,751 km long.**
 
 
• The** India-Nepal border **is open and free for **movement of people and goods**.
 
 
 
• **Pakistan **shares a border with India, which is approximately **3,323 km long.**
 
 
• The India-Pakistan border is also known as the** Line of Control (LoC) **and is heavily militarized due to the **ongoing conflict **between the two countries over the disputed region of Kashmir.

• The dance involves carrying** Kavadi, a semi-circular decorated canopy, **on the shoulders while dancing to the beats of** traditional drums and music. **
 
• The devotees performing Kavadi attam often **pierce their skin** with small hooks or skewers as an act of** penance and devotion.**

• It is a combination of dance, music, dialogue, costume, make-up, and stage techniques.
 
• Yakshagana performances are typically based on Hindu epics and mythology, and they can last for several hours.

• It** **is an important measure of a **country's economic activity and growth**.

questions.question: As per the contents mentioned in Asokan inscriptions, how many major political centres were there in the Mauryan empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** five.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the contents mentioned in Asokan inscriptions, there were** five major political centres **in the **Mauryan empire.** 
 
• The five major political centres of the Mauryan empire were located at** Pataliputra, Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali and Suvarnagiri.**
 
• **Pataliputra:-**
 
 
• It was the capital of the Mauryan empire.
 
• It was located on the Ganges River, and it was a major center of trade and commerce.
 
• Pataliputra was a well-planned city with a grid layout and a variety of public buildings, including palaces, temples, and gardens.
 
 
 
• **Taxila:-**
 
 
• It was located in the northwest of the Mauryan empire, and it was a major center of learning and culture.
 
• Taxila was home to a number of universities and schools, and it was a popular destination for students from all over the world.
 
 
 
• **Ujjain:-**
 
 
• It was located in the central part of the Mauryan empire, and it was a major center of trade and commerce.
 
• Ujjain was also a major religious center, and it was home to a number of temples and shrines.
 
 
 
• **Tosali:-**
 
 
• It was located in the east of the Mauryan empire, and it was a major center of agriculture and commerce.
 
• Tosali was also a major port city, and it played an important role in the empire's trade with other countries.
 
 
 
• **Suvarnagir:-**
 
 
• It was located in the south of the Mauryan empire, and it was a major center of gold mining and trade.
 
• Suvarnagiri was also a major religious center, and it was home to a number of temples and shrines.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asokan inscriptions:-**

 
 
• These are a collection of more than 30 edicts issued by Emperor Ashoka of the Maurya Empire (272-232 BCE).

questions.question: Polyatomic positive ions often have common names ending with the suffix ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-onium.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **-onium:-**

 
 
• It​ is a common suffix for** polyatomic positive ions. **
 
• The "-onium" suffix is used to indicate that a** cation** is composed of** two or more atoms, **such as **ammonium (NH4+) or phosphonium (PH4+)**. 
 
• This naming convention is useful for** identifying and communicating** the composition and charge of **polyatomic ions** in chemical reactions and other contexts. ​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polyatomic ions:-**

 
 
• These​ are ions that consist of **two or more atoms** that are **covalently bonded **or have a **net positive or negative charge.** 
 
• Common examples of** polyatomic positive ions** include **ammonium (NH4+), hydronium (H3O+), and methylammonium (CH3NH3+)**. 
 
 
 
• **"-ium"** :-
 
 
• It is often added to the end of the name of a** polyatomic positive ion** to indicate that it is a **cation (positively charged ion).** 
 
 
 
• **"-ic" :-**
 
 
• **​**It** **is commonly used to indicate the** presence of an acid**, while **"-ous" **is used to indicate a **lower oxidation state** of an element. 
 
 
 
• **"-ide":-**
 
 
• It​ is typically used to indicate an** anion **(negatively charged ion), such as **chloride (Cl-) or oxide (O2-). **

questions.question: A maximum of ______ members can be nominated by the President of India to become the member of the Rajya Sabha.
questions.solution:

• Rajya Sabha:-

 
 
• ​A maximum of **12 members** can be nominated by the **President of India** to become a **member of the Rajya Sabha.**
 
• The Rajya Sabha is the **upper house** of the Indian Parliament and represents the **states and union territories **of India.
 
• The members of the Rajya Sabha are elected or nominated for a term of **six years.**
 
• The nominated members of the Rajya Sabha are usually experts in **various fields** and have the **same powers and privileges** as the elected members. 
 
• The nomination of** members to the Rajya Sabha** is done to ensure that the house has a** diverse representation **of people f**rom different backgrounds and fields.**
 
• The President of India can nominate members to the Rajya Sabha under Article 80(1)(a) of the Constitution of India.
 
• The total strength of the Rajya Sabha is 245, out of which 233 are elected by the legislative assemblies of the states and union territories, and 12 are nominated by the President
